name: Banana Bunchy Top Disease
description: A severe viral disease that causes stunted growth, leaf narrowing, and a characteristic bunchy appearance at the top of the plant. It is transmitted by banana aphids and through infected planting materials.
symptoms: Dark green streaks or hooks on leaf petioles and midribs
Leaves becoming narrow, upright, and brittle
Chlorotic leaf margins with inward curling
Stunted growth with leaves forming a rosette at the top
Plants may produce no fruit or bunches with deformed fingers
causes: Use of infected suckers for planting
Volunteer infected plants serving as virus reservoirs
treatments: Remove and destroy entire infected plant including corm
Inject glyphosate into pseudostem to kill the corm before removal
Control aphid vectors with systemic insecticides
prevention: Use virus-free tissue culture plantlets exclusively
Regular field inspection and early roguing of infected plants
Control banana aphids with neem oil or insecticidal soap
Remove wild banana plants near fields
Use intercropping to reduce aphid landing rates
